1. Problem Statement, Core Bottlenecks & Algorithmic Solutions

❌ Traditional CPU & Tabular Limitations

  • Isolated Row Blindness: Standard models evaluate (amount, time, merchant) without knowing the entity's network neighbors.
  • Memory Bandwidth Bound: Graph aggregation has an arithmetic intensity of << 0.1 FLOP/byte. CPUs spend 95% of cycles waiting on DRAM cache misses (pointer chasing).
  • Power-Law Skewness: Financial hubs (mules/payment gateways) have hundreds of edges, stalling scalar loops.
  • PCIe Transfer Waste: Naive GPU offloading spends 80% time copying memory over PCIe instead of computing.

✅ FraudGraph Intelligence (FGI) Architecture

  • Compressed Sparse Row (CSR): Memory-efficient contiguous arrays (row_ptr, col_idx, features) eliminate pointers and dynamic allocation.
  • Warp-Level Parallel Contraction: 32 threads in a warp aggregate 32-dim features in coalesced 128-byte transactions.
  • Degree-Aware Dispatch: Low-degree nodes run 1 thread/node; high-degree hub nodes run warp/block cooperation with shared memory.
  • Double-Buffered Pinned Streams: cudaMemcpyAsync completely hides PCIe latency behind active computation.
🎓 Professor Viva Question: "Why didn't you just use standard PyTorch Geometric (PyG) or NetworkX?"

Answer: "Sir/Ma'am, standard libraries like NetworkX rely on Python object graphs with heavy pointer overhead (O(N) hash-table lookups). Even framework-level graph libraries like PyG introduce massive autograd and tensor-allocation runtime overhead for simple inference. Our goal in this GPU Capstone was micro-architectural optimization: writing custom bare-metal CUDA C++ kernels, controlling warp coalescing, shared-memory bank conflict avoidance, and asynchronous pinned memory DMA streams directly to solve the memory-bandwidth bottleneck."

2. Core Mechanism: CSR Topology & 4 CUDA Acceleration Tiers

Graph aggregation computes for each node v: h_v = Aggregate(x_u for u in Neighbors(v)), where Aggregate is in {MEAN, MAX, SUM}.

Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) Layout

Instead of an N x N dense adjacency matrix (10,000 x 10,000 = 100 Million floats = 400 MB), CSR requires only:

Array Identifier Data Type & Shape Memory Footprint Functional Role in Kernel
row_ptr int32 (N + 1,) 40.0 KB Index boundaries: Node i's neighbors start at row_ptr[i] and end at row_ptr[i+1]. Degree = row_ptr[i+1] - row_ptr[i].
col_idx int32 (M,) 927.9 KB Contiguous array storing target neighbor node indices u in N(v).
features float32 (N, 32) 1.28 MB Raw transaction node feature vectors (amount, time delta, risk score).
labels int32 (N,) 40.0 KB Ground truth targets: 0 = licit, 1 = synthetic fraud.
timestamps float64 (N,) 80.0 KB Temporal ordering in seconds for causal evaluation (strict non-anticipative policy).

The 4 CUDA Kernel Architectures

Kernel Implementation Source File Micro-Architectural Strategy Tesla T4 Latency
Tier 1: Baseline Global fgi_baseline_kernels.cu 1 thread per node. Iterates through row_ptr range in global memory. Severe memory serialization on hub nodes. 0.0679 ms
Tier 2: Warp-Coalesced fgi_coalesced_kernels.cu 1 warp (32 threads) per node. Threads stride across neighbor list and 32 feature dimensions. Coalesced 128-byte transactions. 0.0612 ms
Tier 3: Degree-Aware fgi_degree_aware_kernels.cu Degree-binning: Low (<32) -> 1 thread; Mid (32–256) -> warp; High (>256) -> block in shared memory. 0.0594 ms
Tier 4: Pinned Streaming main_streams.cu Pinned host memory (DMA) + double-buffered asynchronous streams (cudaMemcpyAsync overlapping compute). 0.0581 ms

Tesla T4 measured latency: sub-0.07ms across Baseline, Coalesced, and Degree-Aware kernels.

⚠️ Professor Tricky Question: "Why did Degree-Aware SUM aggregate have a regression?"

Exact Accurate Answer: "In the degree-aware kernel, high-degree hub nodes utilize Warp 0 performing sequential accumulation across the bin to preserve strict floating-point numerical determinism (avoiding race conditions). This leaves the remaining 7 warps idle in that block for that phase. While MEAN and MAX benefited from fast reduction, SUM suffered under-utilization on hub nodes. This authentic engineering finding is documented in our audit ledger."

🎓 Professor Viva Question: "What is ADR-007? Why is there an omission notice for continuous PR curves?"

Answer: "Architectural Decision Record ADR-007 enforces scientific integrity in imbalanced financial data. In production, an alert threshold tau* must be chosen ahead of time. If we plot a continuous PR curve on test data, we are implicitly peeking at test labels to find thresholds, causing evaluation leakage. Therefore, we froze tau* = 0.1090 strictly on the validation set, evaluated test data blindly, and formally published the ADR-007 Omission Notice."

7. Rapid-Fire Viva Defense Q&A (Top 8 Examiner Questions)

Q1: What is the main research contribution of FraudGraph Intelligence?
Answer: Financial transaction graphs suffer from severe memory-bandwidth bottlenecks (pointer chasing) and power-law degree skewness. Our contribution is a memory-aware CUDA acceleration framework utilizing Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) storage, warp-level coalesced contraction, degree-binning dispatch, and double-buffered pinned memory streams that reduce neighbor aggregation to 0.06 ms while boosting downstream fraud PR-AUC by +7.4%.
Q2: Why did you use Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) instead of an Adjacency Matrix or Edge List?
Answer: An adjacency matrix for 10,000 nodes requires 100 x 10^6 entries (400 MB), 99.8% of which are zeros. An edge list requires random memory lookups for neighbors. CSR stores contiguous arrays (row_ptr and col_idx) in just under 1 MB total, allowing GPU warps to stream contiguous neighbor indices without dynamic memory allocation or pointer chasing.
Q3: How does Warp Coalescing work in your Tier 2 kernel?
Answer: In fgi_coalesced_kernels.cu, instead of 1 thread handling an entire node, 1 warp of 32 threads handles one node. Thread t accesses feature index t across neighbors. Because consecutive threads access consecutive 4-byte floating-point memory addresses, the GPU memory controller collapses the 32 accesses into a single, unified 128-byte cache line transaction, eliminating memory transaction replay penalties.
Q4: Why did MAX neighbor aggregation outperform MEAN for fraud detection?
Answer: Financial fraud is sparse and bursty. If a fraudulent transaction connects to several benign transactions, the MEAN operator averages out the high-risk anomalies, diluting the fraud signal. The MAX operator acts as an extreme-value filter, preserving the maximum suspicious feature magnitude from any neighbor directly into the node's enriched representation.
Q5: What is ADR-007 and why did you omit continuous PR curves on the test set?
Answer: Architectural Decision Record 007 addresses evaluation leakage under extreme class imbalance (3.5%). Plotting a continuous PR curve on test data computes thresholds post-hoc using unobserved labels. To reflect true real-time streaming operations, we chose the optimal threshold tau* = 0.1090 strictly on the validation partition and evaluated test performance as discrete operating points, formally documenting the PR curve omission.
Q6: Why is PCIe transfer overhead a bottleneck and how did you solve it?
Answer: Because our CUDA kernels execute in sub-0.1 milliseconds, standard synchronous cudaMemcpy over the PCIe bus (Gen3/Gen4) takes 3 to 5 times longer than the computation itself. We solved this in Tier 4 (main_streams.cu) using page-locked (pinned) host memory and asynchronous dual CUDA streams, double-buffering transfers so Host-to-Device copying overlaps concurrently with GPU execution of the previous batch.
Q7: How did you verify numerical correctness between CPU and GPU?
Answer: We implemented a strict dual-tolerance verification gate using numpy.allclose() with absolute tolerance atol=1e-5 and relative tolerance rtol=1e-5. Every CUDA kernel output was compared against the CPU 64-bit reference implementation, certifying Zero Drift across all node feature aggregations.
Q8: How does your system handle local Windows machines without NVCC installed?
Answer: Our backend architecture features an authentic fallback design. If local NVCC is absent, local GPU workloads are explicitly cataloged as SKIPPED_CUDA_UNAVAILABLE with zero fabricated measurements, while pre-verified hardware benchmark telemetry from our canonical Google Colab Tesla T4 runner is ingested and displayed with full cryptographic provenance.
